Even `subprocess.run(..., timeout=40)` didn't return within 180 seconds! On TimeoutExpired, `subprocess.run` kills the child (SIGKILL) and then calls `communicate()` again to drain... If the child's *grandchild* (a thread? no) holds the pipe open... `subprocess.run` kills only the direct child. If the python child spawned its own threads — those die with the process.

Hmm wait, `subprocess.run` on timeout: `process.kill()` then `process.wait()`... then re-communicate to collect output. If the killed process was killed successfully, communicate returns. Unless kill() failed silently!? That would mean SIGKILL doesn't work in this container at all — which would also explain BusyBox timeout failing.

Could it be that killing processes is blocked by some seccomp/freazer? That seems drastic. Let me test: can a Python parent kill a child?

Test: parent spawns `sleep 300`; after 3s calls `p.kill()`; measure elapsed.

arguments.command:
cd /app/work && cat > killtest.py <<'PYEOF'
import subprocess, time, sys, os, signal
t0=time.time()

time.sleep(3)
print("before kill", flush=True)
p.kill()
p.wait()
print("after kill elapsed=%.1f rc=%s" % (time.time()-t0, p.returncode), flush=True)

time.sleep(3)
p2.kill(); p2.wait()
print("after kill2 elapsed=%.1f rc=%s" % (time.time()-t0, p2.returncode), flush=True)
PYEOF
